## Summary

Restore the recovered NPC death and boundary-exit phases together.

```text
Enemy damage → drops → pop → infection births ┐
Ally damage  → death sound                   ├→ primary finals → data clear → dead → field callback
Ally outside → drops → pop                   ┘
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** Eight new source-contract regressions fail on master: infection shots follow mine callbacks, allied deaths spread infection, boundary exits omit pop/final callbacks, and births observe an early dead flag/kill count.
  **After:** All eight pass. Shared teardown preserves live data through primary finals, then marks death and records the field callback. Enemy removal remains deferred; ally start/end removal and independent Healer beams retain their existing behavior.
- Two recovered default summon blueprints verify the missing boundary pop. Generalized allied4022 pods retain the source's six hostile mines. Infection Setup RNG precedes mine heading/scatter; transit consumes arguments but rejects insertion before Setup.
- Formatting, TypeScript, **758 unit tests / 7,513 assertions**, production build and **ten distinct affected mock/supplied-SWF browser cases without skips** pass. Actual shell/alpha contact, birth phases, sound events, same-frame boundary expiry and visible damage-death mines are covered; both new galleries were inspected. Existing Healer, crossing, projectile-order and mine cases pass.
- Infection, custom allied pods and outside poses are explicit fixture preconditions. This does not establish ordinary infection reachability, synchronized original audio, all per-part/constructor interleaving or original-runtime/Adobe/full-game parity. These limits remain in the fidelity ledger.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revertible simulation ordering change; no save migration, new dependencies or bundled original media.

**Blast Radius:** combat

Changes NPC death RNG/birth order and boundary sound/callback dispatch. Existing protection, field removal, Healer lifetimes and transit suppression remain covered.
